summary.description: A white, silvery hard metal with magnetic properties, whose compounds are often green in colour. Used extensively in steel manufacturing, batteries, and various industrial applications
environmental_impact: Does not accumulate in fish, plants or animals used for food
Very small amounts essential for normal growth in some species
Unlikely to have immediate effects on local and global environment

top_sdg_impacts.SDG9_Industry_Innovation_and_Infrastruct: Nickel is extensively used in steel manufacturing, batteries, chemical, petroleum and electrical industries, and electroplating. Managing nickel emissions requires industrial innovation to balance its essential role in modern infrastructure development with environmental protection, particularly from mining, refining, and fossil fuel combustion processes.
top_sdg_impacts.SDG3_Good_Health_and_Wellbeing: Nickel poses significant health risks including allergic reactions in 10-20% of the population following prolonged contact, causing skin rashes and potentially asthma. Chronic inhalation exposure to nickel fumes may cause cancer, directly threatening human health and wellbeing, particularly for workers in nickel-related industries.
top_sdg_impacts.SDG12_Responsible_Consumption_and_Produc: Nickel's widespread use in consumer products (jewelry, coins, batteries, steel products) and industrial applications requires responsible production and consumption patterns. The challenge lies in maintaining the benefits of nickel-containing products while minimizing health risks and environmental contamination through improved manufacturing processes and waste management.
